pull.title: feat(routing): drag a fallback chain, and pause one entry without deleting it
pull.body:
## What was missing

**A route rail could only be reordered one arrow press at a time, and never across cards.** The six rails on Model Config draw a route as an ordered path, but the only way to move an entry was its up/down arrows — one press per position — and there was no way at all to move a model from the Sonnet rail to the Opus rail except reading the ref off one card and retyping it into the other. `README.md` said "entries can be reordered" and stopped there, because that was all there was to say.

**And there was no way to take one model out of a route for an hour.** The only tool was the row's `×`: deleting it loses the ordering you spent time building, and the request log stops mentioning the model at all, so you cannot see that it *was* the thing you switched off. Hiding it on the Models page does nothing — that page is documented hide-only and never touches routing (`core/model_visibility.py:18-23`), which is exactly the confusion 5.65.0 closed and this must not re-open.

---

## Design

### Drag: pointer events, one mutator

Pointer events rather than HTML5 drag-and-drop, for a reason rather than a preference. jsdom has neither `PointerEvent` nor a usable `DataTransfer`, so an HTML5 implementation could be written but never covered by the harness this repo tests its UI with; the product's only existing drag (`startModelsDrag`, the Models page) is already pointer-based, and two drag idioms on adjacent pages read as a bug rather than as a distinction; and HTML5 DnD has no touch story at all.

Every gesture — pointer, keyboard, and the existing arrows' promotion path — funnels into **one** `applyRouteDrop(target, ids, copy)`. That is the only function that mutates a chain, so dedupe, the primary swap and the undo snapshot happen in exactly one place. It reuses `ModelChainEditor.swapPrimaryAndFirst()` and `setPrimaryValue()` rather than reimplementing the ordering rules those already own.

Row identity is a stable id (`route:MODEL_OPUS`, `chain:MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS#7`), never the model ref — a ref may legitimately sit on two rails and a fresh row holds none. The selection lives in `state.routeSelection`, never in the DOM, the same rule `test_admin_models_view.py` pins for the neighbouring page. The gap that made cross-rail drag impossible was that **no registry of chain editors existed** — every editor was reachable only through the closure that built it — so `state.routeRails` (chainKey → editor) is new.

The decided semantics, all of them: Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles, Shift-click ranges within one rail, Shift+Space and Shift+Arrow reach the same ranges from a focused grip; a group lands in **rail** order, not click order; a same-rail drop is a move, a cross-rail drop is a copy and Shift at *drop* time makes it a move; a copy onto a chain that already holds the ref **moves the existing row** rather than adding a duplicate the reader would watch vanish on Apply; a copy onto a chain whose primary is that ref is refused with *"Opus already routes to … first"*; a Shift-move may empty a source chain (legal — `BLANK_MEANS_UNSET_FIELDS`) but a primary is never moved out of its own rail, because an empty `MODEL` fails validation and the server refuses to start. Dragging a primary onto its own fallback 1 is the swap its down arrow already performs. The arrows are untouched — they are the WCAG 2.2 single-pointer alternative. Touch drags from the grip only, and `touch-action: none` is scoped to the grip alone (the file's first and only such rule) so a finger still scrolls the card.

Ctrl+Z is depth-1, routing view only, ignored while `document.activeElement` is a text field so it never fights native undo inside a combobox. One drag is one entry — including a nine-row group drop and including both keys a primary swap touches. There is no Discard button; that is its own PR with its own contract test.

### Pause: the benching seam, not the router

The two requirements pull apart in `resolve_chain`: a ref filtered out there never reaches `plan.model_refs()` and therefore gets **no attempt row at all**, so "never executed" and "still visible in the request log" cannot both hold at that line. They can at the 6.14.0 benching seam, so that is where the filter lives:

* `RouteHealthRegistry.usable_indexes(..., paused=...)` drops paused indexes. `_prepare_from` iterates `order`, not `attempts`, so a paused index is never executed and no budget is spent.
* `_AttemptLedger.mark_paused()` beside `mark_benched()`, and it runs **second** — a model that is both benched and paused reads as paused, because the bench is this build's guess and the pause is the operator's decision.
* Pause is **excluded from the "nothing survived" bypass** (`MODEL EJECTION BYPASSED`). Restoring a model somebody paused would be the opposite of what the button says, so an all-paused route returns an empty order and the executor raises a named error instead of quietly re-routing.
* Pause applies even with `FALLBACK_BENCH_ENABLED` off: that switch governs automatic ejection, not one a human flipped.

Everything downstream needed no change — `outcome="skipped"` is already legal, `error_kind` is a free `str | None`, and the detail modal renders the kind verbatim as a chip. `"paused"` appears in the request log with zero JS changes.

Six keys, one per rail: `MODEL_PAUSED`, `MODEL_FABLE_PAUSED`, `MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED`, `MODEL_SONNET_PAUSED`, `MODEL_HAIKU_PAUSED`, `MODEL_VISION_PAUSED`. Pause covers a route's primary *and* its chain, so it is not a property of the chain — hence `MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED` rather than `MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS_PAUSED`. They are never rendered as controls (they are claimed by the routing view so they do not fall into the "anything the manifest adds later" grid as six bare text boxes) and are pruned on write when a ref leaves the route it was paused on — scoped to routes the save actually edited, so an install whose routes live in a repo `.env` does not lose its pauses on an unrelated save.

The write goes through `apply_admin_config_with`, the #223-locked read-derive-write, never a client-side read plus a full replacement — that is precisely the bug #223 fixed. It clears the settings cache and republishes the provider generation, so no restart and no page refetch. `limit_hint()` hardcoded `"Limits & Resilience"`; it is a section→page map now, so a routing error says **Model Config → Model Routing** rather than sending the reader to a page with no such control on it.

One `role=status` panel serves the whole page — drag announcements and pause announcements both — declared statically in `index.html`, whole sentences, `hidden` toggled rather than `style.display`, with Undo and Dismiss.

---

## Verification

**Full suite** — `uv run pytest -q --tb=line`:

```
15 failed, 8080 passed, 38 skipped in 197.68s (0:03:17)
```

The 15 are the documented baseline, unchanged by this PR: 8 websearch tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env` (`test_registry.py` ×5, `test_settings_websearch.py`, `test_web_server_tools.py` ×2), 6 `test_install_ps1_*`, and `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `ty check` all clean.

**jsdom — 29 new tests, every gesture driven in a real document.** The harness now renders the route fields with their real control types (`model`/`optional_model`/`model_chain`) instead of as plain text, so the rails under test are the ones the dashboard actually builds:

```
157 passed in 130.23s   (tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py)
462 passed in 129.82s   (tests/contracts + jsdom, after the layout fix)
```

Covering: grip count == node count with the arrows intact; a press outside the grip reordering nothing; touch on a row scrolling and touch on the grip dragging; reorder; Ctrl-click; Shift-click; Shift+Arrow extending *and shrinking*; Escape; a group drop keeping rail order; cross-tier copy leaving the source intact; Shift-move emptying the source; `changedValues()` naming exactly `MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS` + `MODEL_SONNET_FALLBACKS` after a cross-tier move; a duplicate copy moving the existing row; the primary-is-that-ref refusal; the primary-slot swap and its dirty count of 2; the stranded-primary refusal; Ctrl+Z once and only once; Ctrl+Z inside a combobox doing nothing; the panel's sentence and its `hidden` toggle; **the pause POST carrying exactly one route entry while a drag stays dirty**; a paused row staying visible with its full ref, chip and Resume; the panel's Undo; the calculator's divisor dropping by one; a paused primary; and zero leaked indicator nodes.

**Python — 11 new router/health/ledger tests, 8 new API tests, 17 new contract tests.** Including `test_two_overlapping_pause_writes_both_survive`, which drives two concurrent `apply_admin_config_with` callers — the #223 race was previously covered only by call-count and nothing in `tests/` had ever driven two writers.

**Browser drive (8099 scratch harness, Chrome).** This worktree's `admin_static` served at `/admin/assets/…`, GETs proxied read-only to the live 8082, writes emulated and their bodies recorded. Real routing payload, real model options.

* Selection: `{plainClick: 1, ctrlClick: 2, shiftClick: 4, shiftArrowDown: 5, shiftArrowBack: 4, afterEscape: 0}`, and focus followed the arrow onto the next grip.
* Drag mechanics: exactly **1** drop indicator and **1** `.is-drop-target` card while a drag is live, 0 after it ends.
* Reorder, then Ctrl+Z: the chain returned byte-identical and the dirty counter went `1 unsaved change` → `No changes`.
* Cross-tier Shift-move: `2 unsaved changes`, source emptied, and undo restored both chains exactly.
* Primary swap: *"nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3 is now the Haiku route's model. The previous one, commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free, is fallback 1."*, `2 unsaved changes`, undone cleanly.
* **The Q20 interaction, on the wire.** With a drag dirty, one pause click produced **exactly one** POST: `{"model_key":"MODEL_OPUS","model_ref":"nous_portal/meituan/longcat-2.0:free","paused":true}` — three keys, nothing else — and the dirty drag stayed dirty with its exact value (`opusStillDirty: true`, `1 unsaved change`).
* Apply after a drag posted exactly `["MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS"]`.
* Deadline calculator: Opus went from **8 models to 7** the moment one was paused, with no other route touched.
* **DOM node delta 0.** 6634 nodes before the drag run, 6634 after, 0 stray indicators, 0 stray `is-dragging`/`is-drop-target`.
* 880px breakpoint: every row still one 40px line, no horizontal page scroll, `touch-action` `none` on the grip and `auto` on the row; a touch pointerdown on the row started no drag, on the grip it did.
* **Zero console errors and zero page errors across the entire run** (`list_console_messages` with preserved messages: none).

The first browser pass caught a real defect no test could: `.route-node` and `.route-rail .model-chain-row` are grids with explicit column lists, and three new children wrapped every row's arrows onto a second line while all 462 tests stayed green. Fixed in its own commit — chip and button share one cell (a hidden chip is `display: none` and would vacate a column, shifting every control on a paused row), both grids lead with the same grip and marker columns, and the rail's connector line moved to the marker column's new centre, verified at 44px in Chrome for both a primary and a fallback.

**Live pause proof — isolated server on 8199, redirected fakehome, never `~/.fcc` and never a write to 8082.** Opus primary `commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`, chain `nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3`.

1. Baseline request: `type: message | served by: minimax/minimax-m3-free | text: 'OK'`.
2. `POST /admin/api/config/route-pause` → `paused_key = 'MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED'`, `paused_value = 'commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free'`, and the env file gained `MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED=commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free`. No restart.
3. The very next request, from the request log's own attempt rows:

```
attempt 0 | commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free | outcome= skipped | error_kind= 'paused' | msg= 'paused by you on Model Config'
attempt 1 | nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3       | outcome= failed  | error_kind= 'unavailable' | ...
route_chain = commandcode/minimax/minimax-m3-free,nvidia_nim/moonshotai/kimi-k3
```

The paused model is still in the chain, still in the log, and was never called.

4. With a servable fallback: `type: message | served by: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash | text: 'OK'` — the first *active* fallback served while the primary stayed paused.
5. Both paused:

```
Every model on this route is paused, so there is nothing left to try.
(MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED -- change it on the dashboard under Model Config -> Model Routing)
```

6. Unpaused both: the `MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED` line was removed from the file and the next request came back `served by: minimax/minimax-m3-free | 'OK'`.

---

## Residual risks

* **The dirty-drag / immediate-write interaction** is the sharpest edge here. It is covered on both sides — the browser proves one POST with one route entry beside a dirty drag, and `test_a_pause_write_touches_no_other_setting` proves the env diff is a single added line — but it is the one place where two save models meet on one page.
* **Touch drag is proven in jsdom and in Chrome with a synthetic touch pointer, never on real hardware.** The guard and `touch-action` scoping are right; finger feel is unverified.
* **Six new env keys widen the config surface.** They are in `.env.example`, `docs/USAGE.md` and `README.md`, but no test asserts either file covers every key — the manifest contract is membership-based, never cardinality.
* **`Application._config_lock` is process-local `asyncio`.** Two overlapping pause writes in one server now have a driven test; a second server process editing the same `~/.fcc/.env` is still unserialised, exactly as before this PR.
* **Escape is two steps**: the first abandons a live drag, the second clears the selection. Deliberate — one Escape undoes one intent — but worth knowing.
* Admin screenshots (`/admin/img/admin-model-config.png`) are a manual capture step per `docs/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md`; the rails look different now and the shipped image is stale. Follow-up, not automated against `:8082`.

## Baseline note

`main` at `8a835761` (6.20.0) fails the same 15 tests on this machine before any change: 8 websearch tests that read the developer's real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 `test_install_ps1_*`, and `test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. This branch fails exactly those 15 and no others.

Version: **6.20.0 → 6.21.0** (MINOR — new admin fields and a new capability), with `uv lock` in the same commit.

commit.message:
feat(routing): drag a fallback chain, and pause one entry without deleting it

Two things the Model Config route rails could not do.

Reordering was one arrow press per step, and moving a model from the Sonnet
rail to the Opus rail meant reading the ref off one card and retyping it into
the other. Every entry now has a grip: drag within a card to reorder, Ctrl/Cmd
or Shift-click to pick several, drag onto another tier to copy (Shift to move),
and drop onto a card's top slot to make that model the route's own. Ctrl+Z
undoes one drag. The arrows stay as the WCAG 2.2 single-pointer alternative and
Shift+Space / Shift+Arrow reach the same ranges from the keyboard.

And there was no way to take one model out of a route for an hour. Deleting the
row loses the ordering you spent time on and the log stops mentioning it at all.
Each row now has a Pause button, written immediately through the #223-locked
apply path. A paused ref keeps its place and stays fully on screen, but the
router never tries it: no attempt spent, no deadline consumed -- and it still
gets a request-log row reading skipped / paused, because a route you cannot see
into is a route you cannot debug.

The pause filter sits at the 6.14.0 benching seam (route_health.usable_indexes
plus a mark_paused beside mark_benched) rather than in resolve_chain, which is
the only placement where "never executed" and "still reported" can both hold.
It is excluded from the all-benched bypass -- silently running a model somebody
paused would be the opposite of what the button says -- so an all-paused route
raises a named error instead. limit_hint's page label is a map now, so that
error says Model Config rather than Limits & Resilience.

Pointer events, not HTML5 DnD: jsdom has neither PointerEvent nor a usable
DataTransfer, so an HTML5 drag could be written but never covered, and the
Models page's drag is already pointer-based.

[Files Changed]
- api/admin_static/admin.js: state.routeRails registry, the selection/drag/drop
  functions, one applyRouteDrop mutator reusing swapPrimaryAndFirst and
  setPrimaryValue, depth-1 undo, the pause client, routeNodeControls; grips and
  pause buttons on every rail node; chainLength excludes paused models.
- api/admin_static/index.html: #routeStatus live region; two Guide notes.
- api/admin_static/admin.css: grip, selection, drop indicator, paused row,
  status panel; the file's only touch-action, scoped to the grip.
- api/admin_routes.py: POST /admin/api/config/route-pause.
- config/settings.py, config/admin/manifest.py: six *_PAUSED settings and specs.
- config/admin/values.py, persistence.py: ROUTE_PAUSE_KEYS and pruning on write.
- application/routing.py: plan.paused_refs / plan.paused_env_var, per route.
- application/route_health.py: usable_indexes(paused=...).
- application/execution.py: _all_paused_failure, _AttemptLedger.mark_paused.
- application/deadline_hints.py: page-label map, page_for().
- docs, .env.example, README: the gestures, the six keys, pause vs hide.
- pyproject.toml + uv.lock: 6.20.0 -> 6.21.0 (MINOR: new admin fields and a
  new capability).

[Logic Altered]
Routing resolution is unchanged: a paused ref is still resolved into the plan.
The only behavioural change is in ordering (usable_indexes drops paused
indexes, honours them with benching off, and returns empty rather than
bypassing when all are paused) and in reporting (one extra ledger pass).
An install that pauses nothing routes exactly as 6.20.0 did.

[Verification Method]
Full `uv run pytest -q`: 8080 passed, 38 skipped, 15 failed -- the documented
baseline (8 websearch reading the real ~/.fcc/.env, 6 test_install_ps1_*,
test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache). ruff format,
ruff check and ty clean. 29 new jsdom tests drive every gesture in a real
document; the harness now renders the route fields with their real control
types rather than as plain text. 8 new API tests including two overlapping
writers against the config lock, 11 new router/health/ledger tests, 17 new
contract tests.

[Residual Risks]
The dirty-drag / immediate-write interaction is covered on both sides but is
the sharpest edge here. Touch drag is proven in jsdom and in Chrome, never on
real hardware. Six new env keys widen the config surface.

fix(routing): give the rail an explicit grid column for the grip and pause cell

The route node and the chain row are both grids with a fixed column list, and
the grip, the paused chip and the Pause button were three more children in a
five-column track -- so every row wrapped its arrows onto a second line and the
rail's connector line no longer met its markers. Caught in the browser, not by
a test: the DOM was correct and only the layout was wrong.

Chip and button now share one .route-pause-cell, because a hidden chip is
`display: none` and would vacate a grid column, shifting every control on a
paused row one place left of the same control on the row above it. Both grids
lead with the same 28px grip and 24px marker columns, so a fallback's controls
sit directly under the primary's, and the rail line moves from 12px to 43px --
the centre of the marker column now that the grip precedes it. Verified at
44px in Chrome for both a primary and a fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RnTQRD2QEyAEcEPPahbZu6

docs(agents): record what jsdom can and cannot prove about an admin change

Two things this PR cost time to learn. jsdom proves behaviour and cannot prove
layout, so an admin change that adds elements to a rendered row needs a
browser as well as the harness -- the grid wrap that shipped here passed 462
tests and was obvious in the first screenshot. And an extra child in an
explicit grid track wraps silently, which is worth saying next to it.
